subject: Logging preservation & alerting runbook / evidence for RFP
messages:

Subject: Request: preservation/alerting runbook + evidence for RFP

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of our procurement team’s compliance track (regulated payments, FIN-country coverage), we need a short runbook and sample evidence showing how Redwood preserves and alerts on abuse/misuse signals. Specifically FinovateCorp asked for:

- A simple runbook that describes detection -> alerting -> escalation steps for high-risk policy violations.
- A CSV or sample export of the audit log events we would receive (anonymized ok).
- Confirmation of retention defaults and configurable retention windows (and whether we can set different retention per workspace).
- SLA/target for alert delivery and an explanation of how alerts are routed (email, webhook, PagerDuty).
- Any cryptographic verification / signing of exported logs (to support auditability).

We have an internal deadline of COB 3/16 for the RFP bundle. Can you send something we can include? If you prefer, a short recording + runbook is fine. Also, please cc your solutions engineer who can provide the audit sample.

Best,
Elaine Park
Security Program Manager
FinovateCorp

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@finovatecorp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: preservation/alerting runbook + evidence for RFP

Elaine —

Thanks for the request. Below is the runbook summary and the evidence we’ve attached. I’ve kept each section short so it can be copy/pasted into your RFP response. If you need a formatted Word/PDF version that mirrors your RFP template, tell me which section numbers and I’ll adapt.

1) Runbook (detection -> alerting -> escalation) — summary
- Detection: model runtime flags policy triggers (policy_flag=true), anomaly detector (statistical score > threshold), user-rate anomalies, and manual reports. Events emitted include: event_id, timestamp (ISO8601), request_id, model_id, model_version, input_hash (sha256), output_hash, policy_violation_flag, policy_rule_id, user_pseudonym_id, workspace_id, decision (block/monitor), confidence_score, geo_region.
- Alerting: when event meets high-risk criteria (policy_violation_flag && confidence_score >= 0.85) an alert is generated. Alerts are batched with a max window of 60s for throughput smoothing and then pushed to configured sinks: webhook (signed POST), email, PagerDuty (incident created). For P1 (high-risk with confirmed content match) we target first notification in <= 15 minutes, P2 within 60 minutes.
- Escalation: alerts create a ticket in the customer’s chosen tracker (Webhook -> Customer API). Our default escalation path: automated triage -> 1st on-call (customer-defined) -> Redwood CS escalation if unresolved after 4 hours.

2) Audit/export evidence
- Attached sample (audit-log-sample-202702.csv) contains anonymized rows. Columns included: event_id, ts_utc, request_id, model_id, input_hash, output_hash, policy_flag, policy_rule, decision, workspace_id, actor_type. We anonymize human-identifiable fields by pseudonymization (user_pseudonym_id) and by hashing raw inputs where required.
- Exports can be delivered as: daily partitioned CSV to customer-owned S3 (server-side encrypted), or streamed via Kinesis/Firehose, or via secure (mutual TLS) syslog. Exports are HMAC-signed per-file with an audit header (signature, algorithm, key-id). We can also provide signed manifests for multi-file exports for tamper-evidence during ingest.

3) Retention and redaction
- Default retention: 30 days.
- Enterprise configurable windows: 90 days, 365 days, or up to 7 years by contract.
- Per-workspace policy: yes, separate retention TTLs per workspace (configurable via Console or API).
- Redaction at export: we offer field-level redaction rules prior to export (PII strip, user-hash-only, or full redaction) and can perform reversible pseudonymization keyed to customer KMS for re-identification during audits if required and allowed by policy.

4) SLAs / Alerting targets
- Alert delivery SLA: P1 (critical) <= 15 minutes 95% of the time; P2 <= 60 minutes 98% of the time.
- Notification channels: webhook (recommended), email, PagerDuty. We support multiple endpoints with fallback ordering.
- Monitoring: we provide per-route latency and delivery success metrics visible in Console (token-level) and can stream metrics to Datadog or CloudWatch.

5) Auditability & cryptographic guarantees
- Export signing: HMAC-SHA256 signatures attached to files (key managed in customer KMS via integration), optional PGP signing on request.
- Write-once logs: internal event store writes are append-only; we publish SHA256 manifests for daily partitions to provide tamper proofing.
- Change history: config changes to retention/exports generate audit events and are available via the audit API.

6) Operational playbooks & runbook link
- We’ve attached a concise runbook (redwood_alerting_runbook_v1.pdf) and a sample playbook for suspected automated abuse incidents. Full playbooks (with escalation matrices and contact lists) are provided under enterprise contracts.

7) Additional artifacts attached / links
- Attached: redwood_alerting_runbook_v1.pdf, audit-log-sample-202702.csv, sla-reporting-clause.docx
- Drive link (runbook + long-form evidence): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X_runbook_example
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/67890

If you want a short demo of the export flow (showing S3 export + signature verification), we can run that during a 30-min call. I’ve also put the exact CSV column mapping in the attached runbook appendix.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Laura — this is great and exactly the level we need. Two quick follow-ups from Security Ops:

2) For exports that go to customer-owned S3, will Redwood ever retain a copy on its side after successful delivery? We need confirmation that customer-owned exports are the canonical retention copy if configured as such.

If you can reply here with short answers, we can close the RFP question. Otherwise we’ll schedule the short demo.
